notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-fb70e5, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by Codex, session codex-c83e7a (issue #2166, PR #2268). Source read: arXiv 2502.20645v1, 230 pp., sha256 51d7eacc…5da4e95c, together with its LaTeX source, which is what made the numbering checkable.

Coverage. Every numbered object in this paper shares one counter — theorem environments, plain subsubsection headings, and 93 displays produced by the authors' \numequation/\numalign/\ssinc macros — so I simulated the counters from the source and calibrated the result against the PDF (1.8.6 a display, 1.8.8 a heading, 1.8.10 a definition, 2.3.33 a corollary, 5.1.1 a definition, 7.2.1 a hypothesis, 10.4.1 a lemma). That gives 617 numbered objects. 152 of them are in no item locator, and every one resolves: Theorems 4.1.6 and 4.1.11 and Corollary 4.1.14 are overview restatements whose originals (4.6.45, 4.6.58, 4.6.60, 4.7.1, 4.7.3, 4.7.5) are all covered; Theorems A and B are covered by name; Hypotheses 5.7.1, 5.7.5, 6.3.1 and 7.1.3 are folded verbatim into every dependent item's statement, which is a deliberate and defensible style here; the rest are remarks, notation and cross-references. No missing mathematics was found.

Statuses. All eight library items were opened at the pinned commits — Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474, both available locally — and all fourteen cited declarations exist there, including Condensed.free and Condensed.freeForgetAdjunction (Mathlib/Condensed/Module.lean:51,56), Matrix.symplecticGroup and SymplecticGroup.mem_iff (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SymplecticGroup.lean:101,117), and the Tau Ceti Verma, PBW, comodule, abelian-variety and Cartier-duality declarations. All 32 planned items cite layers that exist and that plan what the item needs.

Routes. All 35 accepted. Eight of the eleven new or Part II identities are already proposed by other papers' routes (Fu-24, Pilloni-20, CDN-20, CDN-20-B, CDN-23, Dospinescu–Le Bras-17, Calegari–Geraghty-20, BCGP-21) and every shared Part II names the same parent as the paper that introduced it; none of the eleven is in an atlas or roadmap file, so `new`/`part-ii` is the right kind throughout. The two pairs of Part IIs that share a parent do not overlap — the briefs assign ownership explicitly. Three Part II titles did not reproduce their parent's title as PROTOCOL section 15 requires; I corrected them in place, adopting BCGP-21's wording for GSp4LocalLanglandsAndGaloisRepresentations. One cross-paper divergence is left for the design job: BCGP-21 routes HigherHidaAndColemanTheory as a new roadmap with a different title, where this extraction and Pilloni-20 make it a Part II of PadicFamilies.

Mistakes in the paper. All 74 recorded findings were checked at their locators and 71 are confirmed, several by computation of my own: #Y(F₂) = 3 and #Y(F₄) = 9 give Q(X) = X⁴+2X²+4 (E041); #C(F₃) = 8 and #C(F₉) = 14 give (X²+2X+3)², so the [2,2,2] row is not 3-distinguished (E053); v₂(α²−1) = 3 for the unit root of X²+X+2 (E050); the counterexamples of E010, E015, E029, E035, E044, E045 and E051 all hold as stated. Three are rejected: E031 records no defect (the printed congruence is correct, merely redundant at p = 2); E047 quotes text that is not at its locator and whose claim is justified by Kisin's local-constancy theorem; E072 asks for more explicit coordinates but identifies no false statement. E017 was confirmed only after correction — the paper prints 'cokernel' correctly on p77, so its recorded quotation was a misreading, but the sentence after it is a literal tautology, and the entry now records that. E035's locator was corrected (7.4.9 is a Definition). One finding was added, E075, a subscript slip in the statement of Lemma 2.7.5. A locator audit over all 74 found that single wrong locator.

Verdict: accept. The extraction is accurate, its routing is consistent with the rest of the atlas, and the corrections needed were small enough to make in place.
